12 A uniform rod of weight 20 N and length 2.0 m is acted upon by two vertical forces, as shown.
15 N
5.0 N
What are the resultant force acting on the rod and the resultant moment about the centre of
gravity of the rod?
resultant moment
resultant force
/ N
/ N m
A
0
10
B
0
20
C
20
10
D
20
20

hints: Notice all three vertical forces: $15\text{ N}$ up at the left end, $5.0\text{ N}$ up at the right end, and the $20\text{ N}$ weight down at the middle of the $2.0\text{ m}$ rod.
For translation use upward positive and downward negative, so compare $(15 + 5.0)\text{ N}$ upward with $20\text{ N}$ downward.

For rotation about the centre of gravity, each end is $1.0\text{ m}$ away, so use $moment = force \times distance$ and check that the left upward force and right upward force tend to turn the rod in opposite senses.
walkthrough: List forces with sign, taking up as positive: $+15\text{ N}$ and $+5.0\text{ N}$ at the ends, and $-20\text{ N}$ for the weight at the centre of gravity.
Resultant force $= 15 + 5.0 - 20 = 0\text{ N}$, so there is no net force for translation.
For moments about the centre of gravity, the weight has zero perpendicular distance so its moment is zero.

Each end is half the $2.0\text{ m}$ length from the centre, so distance $= 1.0\text{ m}$. Left $15\text{ N}$ up gives $15 \times 1.0 = 15\text{ N m}$ one way, right $5.0\text{ N}$ up gives $5.0 \times 1.0 = 5.0\text{ N m}$ the opposite way.
Subtract opposite senses: $15 - 5.0 = 10\text{ N m}$ resultant moment of magnitude $10\text{ N m}$.
Zero resultant force with $10\text{ N m}$ resultant moment matches the row with $0\text{ N}$ and $10\text{ N m}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Upward forces total $20\text{ N}$ which balances the $20\text{ N}$ weight, so resultant force is $0$, and opposite moments $15\text{ N m}$ and $5.0\text{ N m}$ leave $10\text{ N m}$.

B.explanation: Resultant force $0$ is correct, but $20\text{ N m}$ adds the two $1.0\text{ m}$ moments instead of subtracting opposite clockwise and anticlockwise senses.

C.explanation: Resultant moment $10\text{ N m}$ is correct, but resultant force $20\text{ N}$ forgets the $20\text{ N}$ weight acting downwards.

D.explanation: Resultant force $20\text{ N}$ ignores the weight, and $20\text{ N m}$ adds the end moments instead of finding their difference.
